articles.title: How to Deal with Anxiety
articles.summary: Hands down, anxiety is the most common mental health issue affecting Americans today. Over 19% of adults in the U.S. meet criteria for an anxiety disorder in any given year. Many often don’t recognize these difficulties, or mistake them for signs of a physical health condition. As a psychologist, I can tell you that worrying is a normal part of life. articles.title: Ebola’s Death Toll Tops 5,700. Can the Outbreak Be Contained?
articles.summary: The Ebola outbreak that originated in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19 , making it the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history and the second-deadliest worldwide. articles.title: America, China, and the Costs of the Bipolar AI Race
articles.summary: We are in the age of artificial intelligence. Many are comparing the technology to electricity and describing it as the industrial revolution of this century. The United States has long dominated the field, but China’s meteoric rise has made it the strongest challenger to American dominance . The AI race is increasingly bipolar, and much of the power to shape this critical technology is concentrated in these two countries. articles.title: ECT Is a Controversial Treatment of Last Resort. I Wish I’d Gotten It Sooner
articles.summary: Electroconvulsive therapy, or ECT, isn’t terribly fashionable. People sometimes get an uneasy look on their faces at the mention of it. The treatment has come a long way since those agonizing scenes in Miloš Forman’s One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest —but I understand why ECT still freaks people out.
